Summary

Do you love crafting sophisticated solutions to highly complex challenges? As part of our Silicon Technologies group, we would like you to help design and manufacture our next-generation, high-performance, power-efficient processor, system-on-chip (SoC). You'll ensure Apple products and services can seamlessly and authoritatively handle the tasks that make t hem beloved by millions. Joini
ng this group means you'll be responsible for crafting and building the technology that fuels Apple's devices. Together, we will enable our customers to do all the things they love with their devices. As a member of SoC design team, you will be at the center of a SoC design and integration with a critical impact on getting functional products to millions of customers.

Description

As a SOC Design and Integration Engineer, your responsibilities span various aspects of SOC design:

Write microarchitecture and/or design specifications Design, implement, and debug complex logic designs Integrate complex IPs into the SOC Support all front-end integration activities like Lint, CDC, Synthesis, and ECO Work with other engineers that are members of the SOC Design, SOC Design Verification, Emulation, Formal verification, STA, and Physical Design teams. Collaborate with software and systems teams to ensure a high-quality end product.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree + 10 years of experience

Preferred Qualifications

Hands on experience in all aspects of the chip development process with proficiency in front end tools and methodologies.

Experience writing specifications and converting them to design.

Experience with multiple clock domains and asynchronous interfaces.

Experience with AMBA Fabric architecture (AXI, AHB, APB) required

Experience with formal verification techniques desirable

Experience or knowledge of system architecture, CPU & IP Integration, and power and clock management designs desirable.

Ability to communicate effectively across all internal groups.

Familiarity with software and operating concepts a plus.

About Neurophos

The demand for new data centers and AI compute is rapidly outpacing the planet's energy capacity. Digital solutions are hitting a power wall as we approach the physical limits of traditional silicon. Conquering this bottleneck means rethinking the fundamental architecture of inference compute. The industry's current path can't meet the need, so we're taking a different approach.
Instead of traditional electronic circuits, we use silicon photonics and an active, programmable metasurface to perform matrix multiplications at the speed of light. Our optical cells are 10,000x smaller than traditional photonic components, enabling unprecedented density. By using photonics instead of electricity, our chips become more efficient as they scale. This architecture will deliver up to 100 times the energy efficiency of existing solutions while significantly improving performance for large-scale AI inference.

Identify design risks early, evaluate alternative implementations, and drive issues to closure. Contribute to design methodologies, automation, technical documentation, and continuous improvements in ASIC development efficiency.

• Experience with NAND interfaces and protocols, including ONFI or Toggle-mode interfaces, and associated timing and command requirements.

e with your knowledge and skills how things can be done differently. Together, we can change the paradigm of how the world connects

rkloads, identifying bottlenecks across the compute stack, and driving actionable improvements in CPU, memory, fabric, I/O, firmware, OS, compiler, and application behavior. In this role, you will work across architecture, design, software, systems, and partner organizations to evaluate current and future SoC products, build performance insights, and guide product and feature decisions. • Drive workload-based performance analysis for server SoCs, with emphasis on CPU-intensive and system-level workloads.

• Build analytical and empirical models for workload behavior, performance scaling, and feature sensitivity.
• Develop performance projections for internal products and competitive external products.
• Conduct sensitivity studies to hardware and software parameters such as frequency, cache size, memory latency/bandwidth, prefetch behavior, SMT, compiler options, scheduling, and system configuration.
• Identify optimization opportunities across both hardware and software, and drive recommendations to architecture, design, compiler, OS, firmware, and application teams.
• Partner closely with hardware and software organizations to root-cause performance gaps and drive cross-functional optimization plans.
• Define methodologies, metrics, and KPI frameworks for workload analysis, performance tracking, and feature evaluation.
• Use profiling and performance monitoring tools to collect PMU data, hotspot profiles, call stacks, CPI breakdowns, memory behavior, and microarchitectural stall analysis.
• Summarize findings for technical and executive audiences, including architecture tradeoffs, product implications, and competitive positioning.

Qualifications
• PhD in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related field, with 5+ years of industry experience in CPU performance modeling and analysis.
• Deep understanding of CPU microarchitecture, including pipelines, OoO execution, branch prediction, caches, prefetching, SMT, and performance bottlenecks.
• Strong knowledge of SoC-level architecture, including on-chip fabric/interconnect, memory controllers, DRAM systems, coherency, and I/O subsystems.
• Deep understanding of operating systems and compilers, including scheduling, memory management, synchronization, code generation, optimization behavior, and runtime effects on performance.
• Hands-on experience with industry standard performance analysis tools.
• Strong experience in workload analysis, performance characterization, modeling, projection, and optimization for server-class systems.
• Experience enabling and debugging complex server workloads in Linux-based environments.
• Strong analytical, scripting, and data analysis skills for handling large profiling datasets and developing performance models.
• Demonstrated ability to work across organizational boundaries and influence both hardware and software roadmaps through data-driven analysis.

• Experience with pre-silicon performance modeling, simulation, or trace-based analysis.
• Experience with server workloads spanning cloud, enterprise, data analytics, web, database, virtualization, and AI infrastructure.
• Experience with competitive performance analysis and product projection methodologies.
• Familiarity with PMU-based top-down analysis, CPI decomposition, memory subsystem analysis, and sensitivity modeling.
• Experience working with firmware, BIOS, power/performance tuning, and system configuration controls.
• Experience presenting architectural recommendations to senior technical leadership.

What You Will Deliver
• Deep workload characterization of internal and competitive server platforms.
• Performance models and projections for current and future SoC products.
• Clear bottleneck analysis and optimization guidance across HW and SW.
• Sensitivity studies that quantify the impact of key architectural and software parameters.

About QBit Semiconductor

QBit Semiconductor develops advanced System-on-Chip (SoC) solutions for smart imaging, artificial intelligence, and intelligent edge devices. Our technology combines high-performance image processing, always-aware low-power operation, and mixed-signal integration to deliver highly integrated, cost-effective semicond
uctor solutions.

At QBit, engineers have the opportunity to work on sophisticated SoC designs and contribute directly to products from initial architecture and RTL development through silicon implementation and validation.

We are looking for an experienced ASIC / SoC Design Engineer to join our engineering team in Littleton, Massachusetts.

Position Overview

The primary responsibility of this position is the design and development of digital logic at the RTL level. You will participate in the complete SoC development process, including architectural definition, microarchitecture, RTL implementation, simulation, synthesis, integration, and silicon validation.

This is a hands-on engineering role offering exposure to a broad range of SoC technologies and the opportunity to work closely with architecture, design verification, physical design, and silicon validation teams.

Depending on experience and interests, design responsibilities may include:
• Image processing and computer vision accelerators.
• Memory controllers, cache architectures, and memory interfaces.
• DMA engines and high-performance data movement.
• AMBA AXI/AHB interconnects, bridges, and system controllers.
• Standard peripheral and high-speed interface controllers.
• Low-power digital design and clock/reset management.

Key Responsibilities
• Develop and implement digital designs using Verilog and SystemVerilog.
• Participate in architectural definition, microarchitecture, and detailed design specifications.
• Develop, simulate, and debug RTL designs at the block and subsystem levels.
• Collaborate with design verification engineers to ensure functional correctness and verification coverage.
• Support SoC integration, including lint, clock-domain crossing (CDC), and logic synthesis.
• Work with physical design engineers to resolve timing, area, power, and implementation issues.
• Review timing constraints and static timing analysis (STA) results and assist with timing closure.
• Support gate-level simulation and post-silicon debugging and validation.
• Work with third-party IP providers and internal engineering teams to integrate complex SoC subsystems.
• Contribute to design quality, engineering best practices, and successful project execution.

Required Qualifications
• BSEE or MSEE in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field.
• Solid understanding of digital design fundamentals, synchronous logic, state machines, pipelining, and clock/reset architectures.
• Experience with RTL simulation
• Familiarity with the ASIC implementation flow, including synthesis, timing closure, and gate-level simulation.
• Experience with industry-standard EDA tools, preferably Synopsys or Cadence.
• Ability to debug complex design issues and work effectively across engineering disciplines.
• Strong communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to collaborate with globally distributed engineering teams.

Preferred Qualifications
• 5+ years of professional experience in ASIC or SoC digital design.
• Strong proficiency in Verilog and SystemVerilog RTL development.
• Experience in logic synthesis, timing constraints, and static timing analysis.
• Experience with SoC architecture and subsystem integration.
• Familiarity with AMBA AXI/AHB protocols and interconnect architectures.
• Experience with memory controllers, DDR/LPDDR interfaces, or high-speed peripheral interfaces.
• Knowledge of low-power design techniques and clock/power management.
• Experience with design verification methodologies, including SystemVerilog/UVM.
• Familiarity with CDC analysis, RTL lint, and formal verification.
• Programming or scripting experience using Python, Tcl, C/C++, or shell scripting.
• Experience with post-silicon bring-up, lab debugging, and silicon validation.

Why Join QBit?

At QBit, you will be part of a highly experienced engineering organization developing sophisticated semiconductor products.

Unlike highly specialized roles at larger companies, our engineers have the opportunity to work across multiple aspects of SoC development, take ownership of meaningful design challenges, and see their work progress from RTL to working silicon.

We offer a collaborative engineering environment where technical contributions matter and engineers have direct involvement in product development.

• Collaborative and technically challenging work environment.

NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It's a unique legacy of innovation that's fueled by great technology-and amazing people. We are seeking a Senior SoC Subsystem & I/O Architect to join our ambitious LPU team. • Define high-level SoC subsystem architecture for LPU products.
• Convert LPU product requirements into architectural specifications for uncore, IO, memory, firmware-facing, boot, reset, safety, fault tolerance, diagnostic, and power regulation subsystems.
• Collaborate intimately with IP teams to develop detailed build documents for PCIe/CXL, NVLink/NVLink-C2C, UCIe, AXI/CHI, NoC fabrics, memory controllers, coherency blocks, MMUs/IOMMUs, boot, reset, and associated SoC infrastructure.
• Specify subsystem behavior encompassing enumeration, capability discovery, configuration flows, sequence control of memory operations, data consistency, address mapping, interrupt handling, virtualization, error handling, and firmware/software-visible controls.
• Build or guide functional and architectural models from specifications, using C++, SystemC, Python, or similar languages.
• Use models to validate architecture intent, subsystem behavior, configuration sequences, and IP interactions before RTL or silicon is available.
• Drive tradeoffs across bandwidth, latency, power, area, timing, scalability, reliability, security, debuggability, and software usability.
• Review IP specifications, subsystem architecture documents, model behavior, verification plans, and validation strategies.
• Collaborate with architecture, IP, firmware, software, RTL, verification, platform, and post-silicon teams to bring architecture decisions to completion.

• Extensive understanding of IO and interconnect cores including PCIe, CXL, NVLink, NVLink-C2C, UCIe, AXI, CHI, or NoC fabrics.
• Experience working from product requirements to architecture requirements and IP/subsystem specifications.
• Experience crafting functional models, architectural models, golden models, or C/SystemC models from architecture specifications.
• Solid grasp of memory ordering, coherency, address translation, interrupts, virtualization, MMUs/IOMMUs, enumeration, configuration, and error management.
• Solid knowledge of boot, reset, firmware handoff, capability discovery, security, RAS, debug, and power-management architecture.
• Strong communication abilities and capability to harmonize architecture decisions across IP, firmware, software, verification, and product groups.

• Hands-on experience with LPU, GPU, CPU, AI accelerator, chiplet, or multi-die SoC architecture.
• Extensive knowledge in PCIe/CXL, NVLink/NVLink-C2C, UCIe, AXI/CHI, coherent fabrics, NoCs, or chip-to-chip links.
• Extensive knowledge in formulating architecture specifications for advanced SoC subsystems.
• Experience building executable functional models directly from product, architecture, or protocol specs.

This is a highly integrated 5G NR NTN modem System-on-Chip designed for satellite and non-terrestrial network (NTN) infrastructure digital communications SOC
Sitting at the intersection of product engineering, test engineering, and validation engineering, you will guide the modem SOC from tape-out through qualification, characterization, engineering validation, and high-volume production-directly influencing schedule attainment, yield, and cost structure
Your work will contribute to Blue Origin's mission of enabling millions to live and work in space by advancing TeraWave's space-based broadband communication architecture
Travel expected up to 10% of the time
Take full ownership of the Modem SOC product release, guiding the chip from tape-out compliance through production qualification while ensuring adherence to internal development processes and JEDEC standards
Formulate and execute characterization and qualification plans across all major subsystems
Drive Validation and test engineering groups for measurements and data collection, and own statistical analysisqualification, ATE correlation, production test-limit setting, and datasheet parameter validation
Work collaboratively with the validation team towards the delivery of a fully characterized and tested SoC
Lead boot subsystem bring-up and validation: secure boot, QSPI NOR flash, EMMC NAND flash, root-of-trust authentication flows, and OTA firmware update verification
Own power domain and DVFS characterization: power-mode transitions, per-domain voltage/frequency scaling, power gating, wake/sleep latency, and GALS clocking architecture validation for space mission power budgets
Lead L2/L3 crypto DMA and security subsystem validation: M2M crypto throughput, key management, interrupt routing, and integrity-fail response
Develop and validate ATE test plans and coverage in partnership with test engineers, including DFT-based structural test (scan, BIST, JTAG) and functional test coverage for modem PHY and compute subsystems
Own failure analysis across the production lifecycle-coordinating with design, OSATs, and labs to root-cause yield, reliability, and field issues and to drive corrective actions

Application close date:
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We're working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapt
ers to the history of spaceflight!

Blue Origin is pioneering the future of space-basedconnectivitywithTeraWave, a revolutionary satellite communications network designed to deliver symmetrical data speeds of up to 6Tbpsanywhere on Earth.This network will service tens of thousands of enterprise, data center, and government users who require reliable connectivity for critical operations.

We are seeking a seasoned Senior Product Engineer to own the production release of the Modem SOC for TeraWave. This is a highly integrated 5G NR NTN modem System-on-Chip designed for satellite and non-terrestrial network (NTN) infrastructure digital communications SOC. Sitting at the intersection of product engineering, test engineering, and validation engineering, you will guide the modem SOC from tape-out through qualification, characterization, engineering validation, and high-volume production-directly influencing schedule attainment, yield, and cost structure. Your work will contribute to Blue Origin's mission of enabling millions to live and work in space by advancing TeraWave's space-based broadband communication architecture.

Special Mentions:
• Relocation provided
• Travel expected up to 10% of the time
• Interviews will include a technical assessment
• This role is based onsite in Austin, TX. A temporary remote work exception is approved while our Austin site isbeing developed.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to
• Take full ownership of the Modem SOC product release, guiding the chip from tape-out compliance through production qualification while ensuring adherence to internal development processes and JEDEC standards.
• Formulate and execute characterization and qualification plans across all major subsystems.
• Drive Validation and test engineering groups for measurements and data collection, and own statistical analysisqualification, ATE correlation, production test-limit setting, and datasheet parameter validation.
• Work collaboratively with the validation team towards the delivery of a fully characterized and tested SoC
• Lead boot subsystem bring-up and validation: secure boot, QSPI NOR flash, EMMC NAND flash, root-of-trust authentication flows, and OTA firmware update verification.
• Own power domain and DVFS characterization: power-mode transitions, per-domain voltage/frequency scaling, power gating, wake/sleep latency, and GALS clocking architecture validation for space mission power budgets.
• Lead L2/L3 crypto DMA and security subsystem validation: M2M crypto throughput, key management, interrupt routing, and integrity-fail response.
• Develop and validate ATE test plans and coverage in partnership with test engineers, including DFT-based structural test (scan, BIST, JTAG) and functional test coverage for modem PHY and compute subsystems.
• Own failure analysis across the production lifecycle-coordinating with design, OSATs, and labs to root-cause yield, reliability, and field issues and to drive corrective actions.
• Review NPI hardware designs-load boards, characterization boards, and probe cards-for modem SOC bring-up.
• Spearhead cost reductions through yield improvement, test-time optimization, and ATE coverage rationalization.
• Manage excursions, including low-yield events, RMAs, and in-field anomalies.
• Operate as the key interface between the NPI team and backend operations and OSATs.
• Define KPIs for modem SOC production health, monitor ongoing performance, and deliver regular reporting to program and operations leadership.
• Continuously identify process enhancements for the NPI flow, with emphasis on modem-specific bring-up complexity across compute, modem PHY, and high-speed interface domains.
• Act as a mentor to junior team members, fostering technical and professional growth.

Minimum Qualifications:
• BSEE or equivalent and 7+ years of IC product engineering / product development experience, including bringing complex digital or mixed-signal SOCs from definition to production release.
• Demonstrated experience owning product releases through characterization, qualification, and reliability testing on advanced-node ASICs.
• Hands-on expertise with high-speed digital SOC testing: SerDes interface characterization, DDR memory validation, compute subsystem bringup, and ATE test development.
• Advanced knowledge of IC manufacturing processes, DFT methodologies (scan, BIST, JTAG), and failure analysis techniques.
• Strong statistical analysis capability with proficiency in JMP, Gauge R&R, limit setting, and DOE methodology.
• Proficiency in Python or similar scripting language for test automation, data collection, and analysis.

Preferred Qualifications:
• MSEE or advanced degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field.
• Extensive experience with compute SOC or modem ASIC NPI, including ownership of schedule, planning, and budget.
• Deep expertise in 5G NR modem PHY testing or validation in satellite / NTN applications, including L1 channelization, beam-slice datapath, and full-duplex TX/RX characterization.
• Hands-on experience with 112G PAM4 SerDes characterization: eye diagram analysis, jitter decomposition, BER floor testing, and daisy-chain link margin.
• Direct experience with LPDDR5x or LPDDR6 bring-up, ECC validation, throughput characterization, and margin testing.
• Experience with Arm compute subsystem NPI: Neoverse core bringup, CMN-700 mesh, SMMU/GIC validation, and interrupt subsystem verification.
• Experience with secure boot validation, root-of-trust authentication flows, and hardware security module testing.
• Experience with timing and synchronization interface validation: PPS, PTP/IEEE 1588, SyncE, or GNSS reference inputs.
• Experience with DVFS and multi-domain power management testing for advanced-node SOCs.
• Experience developing or qualifying radiation-tolerant / radiation-hardened products for space applications.
• Direct experience interfacing with OSATs and backend operations through NPI bringup and production ramp for advanced-node digital or mixed-signal ASICs.
• Experience mentoring early-career engineers.
